body:
You could use initializer lists here: 
```c++
p_gizmo->add_handles(Vector({ start_position, end_position }), handles_material);
```
More concise, I will do that ! Thanks !

Prefer a more explicit naming like `lines_ptrw` instead of just `ptr` as most code views and reviews happen on (web) git without an IDE crutch at hand.

The name makes it clear when skimming over the code base what Vector / LocalVector it is and the ptr / ptrw at the end makes it clear if it is a read or write pointer instead of constantly having to scroll to look it up.

The macros are making the code a bit hard to read, imo. How about this?
```c++
    for (Vector3 &_position : { start_position, end_position }) { 
        [...]
    }
```

I think that should amount to about the same general speed.
This should be `real_t`, as should some other variables you added.
This is a magic number corresponding to the quality / smoothness of the circle, right? If so, it should be static constexpr, and be commented that it can be changed to adjust the circle smoothness.
I kept float because previous code was using float in the loop, but it could be `real_t`, I will change it
True, a comment wouldn't hurt. Thanks

I do agree that it is not ideal to read, but I'm not sure this is really better, as the main offender is the block of `push_back`, and it will still be there. And this has some _very small_ cost while the macro has none. If other people feel the same way, then I'll change it, as it will hardly matter (the optimizer will unroll it anyway, but why give the compiler work )
Yeah sorry, i meant assignment block (forgot I removed the push_back ...). Macros are real code too you know, but I understand the feeling.  I'll leave it like this for now.
